subject: Service territory confirmation & private endpoint operator roster
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@medicore.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: IT Ops <itops@medicore.com>, Legal <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Region commitment for pilot + operator roster request

Hi Stephanie,

As part of our procurement checklist for the POC, we need a brief confirmation that Redwood can guarantee that inference for our pilot (Medicore Pilot ID: MP-2027-08) will be served from US-only regions and that any private endpoint (VPC/privatenet) will be restricted to the operator set we designate.

Can you:
- Confirm which US regions (primary + standby) will host our inference workload for the pilot.
- Provide the current list of operator/service accounts that will have access to the private endpoint. We only need names and email addresses; a CSV is fine.
- Attach any short statement you have for customers around geo-commitment for pilots (SOC2/CAIQ references welcome).

We need this to complete our internal security sign-off by Friday EOD.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of IT Security, Medicore Health

---
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@medicore.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region commitment for pilot + operator roster request

Marta — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers first:

1) Regions: Primary: us-west-2 (Oregon). Standby / failover: us-east-1 (N. Virginia). We will not route EU or APAC traffic for this pilot unless you request cross-region failover.

2) Operator roster: we can produce a CSV with the exact operator/service accounts that have NAT-level or KMS access to the private endpoint. I asked Ben to pull the current list and Grace to validate ACLs.

3) Geo/commitment statement: attaching a short PDF that references our SOC 2 coverage and our CAIQ-mapped controls for data residency. It includes the specific controls we rely on for regional isolation and our private endpoint operator model.

Next steps / ask from you:
- Confirm you’re happy with the two-region plan above.
- Confirm whether you require an operator-level NDA or a restricted-operator agreement template before we share personnel names.

I’m attaching the geo statement now and will follow up with the CSV once Ben sends it.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: geo-commitment-statement.pdf

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region commitment for pilot + operator roster request

Stephanie / Grace — pulling operator list now. Current snapshot (pre-redaction) includes:
- infra-ops@redwood.com (Service Account)
- keystore-ops@redwood.com (Service Account)
- aaron.li@redwood.com (Oncall Engineer)
- priya.n@redwood.com (Deployment Lead)
- sec-sre@redwood.com (SRE Team Alias)

I’ll scrub emails and produce operator_roster.csv with columns: name, role, email, privilege-level, justification.

Note: per our standard operator policy, only service accounts and named on-call engineers have network/KMS access to private endpoints; CS and sales roles are explicitly excluded.

Attaching a quick connectivity diagram and the roster CSV once scrubbed.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: operator_roster.csv, connectivity-diagram.png

---
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@medicore.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region commitment for pilot + operator roster request

Marta — attached is the scrubbed operator_roster.csv and a connectivity diagram. Key notes inline:
- The roster includes 5 entries: 2 service accounts and 3 named engineers. Each entry has a short justification and the privilege level we enforce (NET/KMS/APP).
- Access control model: private endpoint sits in your VPC peering connection; operator accounts are constrained via mutual TLS + short-lived IAM tokens.
- Auditability: we log operator activity to our audit stream (retention 13 months), and can provide a filtered CSV of operator activity for the pilot if Medicore needs it.

Please confirm whether you want the engineers redacted and replaced with role-only placeholders, or whether Medicore legal is comfortable receiving the names under the existing partner agreement.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Attachments: operator_roster.csv, connectivity-diagram.png

---
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@medicore.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: IT Ops <itops@medicore.com>, Legal <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region commitment for pilot + operator roster request

Stephanie — this is perfect, thank you. We reviewed the region plan and the operator roster with IT Ops and Legal. Two quick confirmations:

- Medicore accepts the primary/standby regions as us-west-2 / us-east-1 for the POC and understands there will be no EU/APAC routing.
- Legal prefers receiving the roster with names redacted and role-only placeholders for the pilot. We will request full named roster only after we execute the partner operator addendum (a short SOW amendment).

If you can resend operator_roster.csv with the engineer names replaced by role placeholders (e.g., Oncall Engineer #1) we’ll mark the security gate as closed and proceed to sign the SOW.

Appreciate the responsiveness — please send the redacted CSV and we’ll close out.

Best,
Marta
